raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming these 12 mu for 30 years now, same wheat-maize rotation like everyone else around here. With ten mouths to feed in the household — though a couple of the young ones are working in town now — I can't afford to gamble, but I also can't afford a bad harvest.

**For the wheat coming up in October:**

I'll plant around October 10-15, right after I clear the maize. I use the Jimai variety — my cousin down the lane has been getting good results with it, and the agri-supply shop in town has it in stock. I'll buy fresh seed, about 15 kg per mu, costs me maybe 45 yuan per mu. I don't save my own seed anymore — the extension guy said purchased seed gives better stands, and I've seen that's true.

Fertilizer is my biggest worry because urea went up again this year. I'll put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 40 kg per mu before planting. Then I topdress with urea at jointing in March, maybe 15 kg per mu. That gives me around 16 kg N per mu total. The extension station told us 14-15 is the target, but I like a bit of extra — yellow wheat in April makes me nervous. I'll check the field at jointing; if it looks strong I won't add more.

Irrigation: I'll do the winter water in late November to help the wheat overwinter, then jointing water in late March, then grain-filling water in early May. Three times. Well water costs me about 20 yuan per mu each time for pumping — that adds up. If it rains good in spring I might skip one, but last year was dry so I'm not counting on rain.

I'll spray herbicide once in spring for the cleavers and shepherd's purse, and watch for aphids in May. If I see powdery mildew I'll spray once, otherwise I won't bother.

For labor, my wife and I plus my older brother can handle planting. I'll hire the combine harvester in June — 60 yuan per mu but it saves us a week of work and the wheat goes straight in the bag.

I'm hoping for about 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 460, year before 420 because of the late frost. Middle of the road is what I plan for.

**For the maize right after wheat in June:**

This is the tight part. Combine comes through on June 10-12, and I need maize in the ground by June 15 at the latest or I lose yield. I use direct seeding — no tillage, just drill it straight into the wheat stubble. A neighbor and I share a no-till seeder, saves renting one.

I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid — it's been reliable for 10 years around here. About 30 yuan per mu of seed at 2 kg per mu.

Fertilizer on maize I keep simpler than wheat. I put down a slow-release compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, plus urea side-dressed at the big bell stage (V10 or so), another 15 kg urea. Total N around 15-16 kg per mu. Maize needs less water and less fuss than wheat if the summer rains come.

Irrigation: usually one watering in late July if it's a dry summer, maybe two if the rain doesn't show. Last two summers I only irrigated once each. If the monsoon is late like they're saying, I might need two.

Spray herbicide right after planting, before the maize comes up — that's the main weed control. Watch for corn borer in August, spray once if I see the leaf damage.

Expect about 500 kg per mu. Good year I've hit 550, bad year 420.

**Overall**: My cash is tight because fertilizer prices are up. I'm keeping my rates close to last year but not cutting — cutting N is how you lose 100 kg per mu, I've seen neighbors do it and regret it. My ten-person household means food security matters — even if wheat prices drop I still want the grain for the family. Two sons send money from their factory jobs, which helps with the input purchases in the fall.
